title: In Confronting China, The West Needs Partners in Southeast Asia
gist: The author argues the West should prioritize Southeast Asian partners at the November 10 ASEAN summit in Manila, using the extra time from the extended US-China trade truce, while Europe grows more willing to confront Chinese trade practices. The excerpt is truncated.

themes.theme: ASEAN and the China trade truce

insights.claim: The ASEAN summit in Manila on November 10 falls on the date the China-US trade truce was set to expire, and the September 24 Xi-Trump summit's one tangible result was extending the truce.
insights.speaker: Alexandru Filip
insights.so_what: Truce extension buys time; watch the November 10 ASEAN summit for US positioning.

insights.claim: The author argues that Western efforts to reindustrialize and regain market share from China's unsustainable trade practices should not compromise economic partnerships with Southeast Asian countries.
insights.speaker: Alexandru Filip
insights.so_what: Supply-chain diversification beneficiaries are Southeast Asian economies, if the West avoids blanket trade barriers.
